def-qsmx-quantum-potts-hamiltonian:
## Definition

Let $Q\in\{2,3,4\}$ and let $L\geq1$ be an integer. The finite Potts-clock space is
$$\mathcal H_{Q,L}:=(\mathbb C^Q)^{\otimes L}$$
with its standard tensor-product Hermitian inner product and computational orthonormal basis
$$|a_1,\ldots,a_L\rangle:=|a_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes|a_L\rangle,\qquad a_j\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}.$$
On one site use the clock and shift convention
$$R_Q|a\rangle=e^{2\pi i a/Q}|a\rangle,\qquad M_Q|a\rangle=|a-1\!\!\pmod Q\rangle.$$
Set $|+\rangle:=Q^{-1/2}\sum_{a=0}^{Q-1}|a\rangle$. For $1\leq j\leq L$, let $P_j$ be $|+\rangle\langle+|$ on factor $j$ and identity on every other factor. For $1\leq j<L$, let
$$D_{j,j+1}:=\sum_{a=0}^{Q-1}|aa\rangle\langle aa|$$
act on factors $j,j+1$ and as identity on the others. The open-chain Temperley-Lieb operators are
$$e_{2j-1}:=\sqrt Q\,P_j\quad(1\leq j\leq L),\qquad e_{2j}:=\sqrt Q\,D_{j,j+1}\quad(1\leq j<L).$$
Equivalently, these are the exact clock-shift operators of the open Potts representation: $e_{2j-1}=Q^{-1/2}\sum_{r=0}^{Q-1}M_{Q,j}^{\,r}$ and $e_{2j}=Q^{-1/2}\sum_{r=0}^{Q-1}R_{Q,j}^{\,r}R_{Q,j+1}^{-r}$. Thus there are $2L-1$ operators and no bond from site $L$ back to site $1$.

For real coefficients $J_1,\ldots,J_{2L-1}$, define the weighted open-chain matrix
$$H_{Q,L}(\mathbf J):=-\sum_{i=1}^{2L-1}J_i e_i.$$
For a self-adjoint finite matrix $H_{Q,L}$ and real $\beta$, let $\Lambda(H_{Q,L})$ be its finite set of distinct eigenvalues and let $\Pi_\lambda$ be the orthogonal projection onto the $\lambda$-eigenspace. Define
$$B_\beta(H_{Q,L}):=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda(H_{Q,L})}e^{-\beta\lambda}\Pi_\lambda,\qquad Z_\beta:=\operatorname{tr}B_\beta(H_{Q,L}),\qquad \rho_\beta:=Z_\beta^{-1}B_\beta(H_{Q,L})$$
whenever $Z_\beta>0$. Here a density matrix means a self-adjoint positive semidefinite endomorphism of trace one. The A-page Gibbs lemma establishes that the displayed $H_{Q,L}$ is self-adjoint and that $Z_\beta>0$ for every finite real $\beta$.
lem-qsmx-potts-finite-gibbs-density:
## Statement

For $Q\in\{2,3,4\}$, $L\geq1$, real coefficients $J_i$, and finite real $\beta$, the matrix $H_{Q,L}(\mathbf J)$ defined on the Potts-clock chain is self-adjoint. With the spectral definitions $B_\beta$, $Z_\beta$, and $\rho_\beta$ from that definition, $Z_\beta>0$ and $\rho_\beta$ is a positive semidefinite matrix of trace one. This is a finite-dimensional mathematical fact; it makes no thermodynamic-limit or empirical claim.
thm-qsmx-potts-tl-and-hecke:
## Statement

Let $Q\in\{2,3,4\}$, $L\geq1$, $\delta:=\sqrt Q$, and let $q\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ satisfy $q+q^{-1}=\delta$. Use the $2L-1$ open-chain operators $e_i$ defined for this Potts-clock chain, and put $g_i:=qI-e_i$ for $1\leq i\leq2L-1$. Then $u_i\mapsto e_i$ represents the rank-$2L$ Temperley-Lieb algebra $P_{2L}(\mathbb C,\delta)$, and
$$(g_i-qI)(g_i+q^{-1}I)=0,\qquad g_ig_{i+1}g_i=g_{i+1}g_ig_{i+1},\qquad g_ig_j=g_jg_i\quad(|i-j|>1).$$
These are the type-A Hecke relations in the normalized generator convention after the coefficient specialization $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. The specified clock-shift model selects $q=e^{i\pi/4},e^{i\pi/6},1$ for $Q=2,3,4$, respectively. At $Q=4$, $q=1$ and the same operators $g_i=I-e_i$ satisfy the symmetric-group Coxeter relations, so they define an action of $S_{2L}$. No faithfulness, semisimplicity, or unitarity is asserted.
thm-qsmx-spin-singlet-exchange-interface:
## Statement

Let $N\geq1$ and let $\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$ have the standard tensor-product Hermitian inner product, linear in its first argument, with $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ orthonormal on each factor. For $1\leq i<N$, let $s_i$ be the swap of tensor factors $i,i+1$, let $|\omega\rangle=(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)/\sqrt2$, and let $P_i=I^{\otimes(i-1)}\otimes|\omega\rangle\langle\omega|\otimes I^{\otimes(N-i-1)}$ be the projection onto this singlet on those two factors. Put $e_i:=I-s_i$. Then these are the loop-weight-two Temperley-Lieb generators. In the Hecke normalization $g_i(q):=qI-e_i$, at $q=1$ one has $g_i(1)=s_i$. For arbitrary real coefficients $\mathcal J_i$, the finite exchange sum
$$X_N(\boldsymbol{\mathcal J}):=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathcal J_i s_i$$
satisfies
$$X_N(\boldsymbol{\mathcal J})=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathcal J_i\right)I-\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathcal J_i e_i.$$
The equality $g_i(1)=s_i$ is internal to this spin-half representation; it does not identify its state space with the distinct $Q=4$ Potts representation.
